key_insight: An agentic system discovers simple symbolic inventory policies by separating LLM-driven formula design from numerical parameter fitting.
engineering_relevance: Compact replenishment formulas could improve inventory decisions across operational settings without elaborate online computations.
method: LLMs revise symbolic policies within explicitly defined formula and template classes.
A numerical engine fits parameters per instance and evaluates policy performance.
Multicriteria selection, operational diagnostics, and reusable motifs guide a three-stage search for shared templates.
evidence_signal: Across 15,600 instances spanning 50 demand distributions, discovered templates improve aggregate empirical performance over evaluated simple-formula benchmarks; a conditional theorem establishes strict superiority over a specified capped base-stock class.
watch_item: The theoretical guarantee applies only to a specific three-period lead-time setting under stated demand and cost conditions, and deployment still requires instance-specific parameter fitting.
paper_title: Agentic Discovery of Simple Symbolic Inventory Policies
